articles.headline: Colts officially place WR Alec Pierce on IR with heel issue
articles.description: The Colts officially placed receiver Alec Pierce on injured reserve Saturday, starting the clock on a potential return as he attempts to rehab and rejoin the lineup.
articles.body:
INDIANAPOLIS -- The Indianapolis Colts officially placed receiver Alec Pierce on injured reserve Saturday, starting the clock on a potential return as he attempts to rehab and rejoin the lineup.

Pierce sustained a reinjury of a heel issue during Sunday's overtime loss to the Kansas City Chiefs, leaving the game late in the first quarter, unable to put weight on his left leg.

Pierce had surgery in March, his rehab keeping him sidelined through the preseason. He returned on a limited basis in Week 1 and lasted just a few plays into the Colts' Week 2 game.

Now, after consultation with multiple physicians, Pierce and the Colts will work to rehab the foot with a goal of returning this season. Surgery, so far, has not been discussed by any of those physicians, a team source told ESPN.

Pierce must now miss a minimum of four games after being placed on IR. The earliest he could return to the lineup would be the Colts' Oct. 25 game at the Minnesota Vikings.

The loss of Pierce -- who is one of the league's premier deep threats and has led the NFL in yards per catch in each of the past two seasons -- could have a significant impact on the Colts. With Pierce playing just 41% of the team's snaps in the first two weeks, quarterback Daniel Jones saw a noticeable drop-off in his yards per attempt; he is averaging 6.1 after a career-best 8.1 last season.

The effort to replace Pierce continued Saturday. The Colts signed veteran and longtime Giants receiver Darius Slayton earlier this week. Then, Saturday, they signed receiver Anthony Gould from the practice squad. The Colts also elevated Nick Westbrook-Ikhine from the practice squad for Sunday's game against the Houston Texans.

articles.headline: 2026 NBA free agency: Grades for offseason signings, extensions
articles.description: We're grading the biggest free agent signings and extensions, including Steph's new two-year deal.
articles.body:
The NBA offseason is here, and teams across the league have been busy making moves. Free agency officially began June 30.

I'm grading every free agent signing and the most impactful extensions this offseason, breaking down the ramifications for all teams and players involved.

To determine each grade, I'm looking at multiple factors, including the player's on-court impact and age, the contract's financial implications and the context of the team's short- and long-term outlooks. How risky or certain is the move? And how much does it help or hurt the team's chance to win a championship, next season or beyond?

Let's get into the latest moves:

Quick links: 

Trade grades | Latest buzz | Trade machine

Depth charts | Trade tracker | More coverage

Sept 25: Curry agrees to two-year extension

Stephen Curry terms: Two years, $116 million (player option in year two)

Grade: B

"I'll make the decision when I'm ready," Curry told ESPN's Anthony Slater earlier this week, about his timeline for signing a new contract extension. Evidently, Curry didn't take much longer to get ready.

Curry's new contract is a win for the Golden State Warriors in two ways. First, it locks up the Warriors legend for an extra two years, as he was poised to enter free agency next summer without a new deal. Second, he's taking a pay cut and signing for $20 million less than his maximum allowed amount, which could be crucial for a team that's trying to add -- and afford -- more star power next to him.

For the moment, Curry's new deal keeps max cap space open for the Warriors next summer. However, that theoretical figure doesn't include Brandin Podziemski's cap hold, Kristaps Porzingis' mostly nonguaranteed contract, or extensions for Jimmy Butler III and Draymond Green, who are both free agents after this season.

In that sense, a larger pay cut for Curry -- more akin to the two-year, $90 million deal Kevin Durant signed with the Houston Rockets last year -- would have been even better for the Warriors. But it's difficult to fault Curry for not taking so drastic a diminishment when he remains the Warriors' best player, even in his late 30s, and an extra $10 million per season is still beneficial for Golden State.

The one real concern about this extension from the Warriors' side is whether Curry will still be worth roughly a third of the salary cap as he approaches his 40th birthday.

He remains a singular offensive force when he's on the court, even if he's no longer producing like he did at his peak. Yet the injuries are mounting. Curry played just 43 games last season, and he has reached 65 games -- the threshold for many major award consideration -- just twice since 2018-19. Those two seasons came in 2023-24 and 2024-25, to be fair, so he has a recent history of health. But players typically don't become more available as they age, so it's worth wondering whether Curry's half-season absence last year is an unfortunate omen.

articles.body:
NBA free agency has almost reached the end, with several players landing in new homes this offseason.

LeBron James decided to continue his historic career with the Philadelphia 76ers after months of deliberation. The Sixers also traded for Jaylen Brown this summer, turning the franchise into a true contender with two huge moves.

Meanwhile, Giannis Antetokounmpo is headed to South Beach to team up with Bam Adebayo and the Miami Heat, and the Los Angeles Lakers have been sold for the second time in 10 months.

What will happen next during this turbulent offseason?

Check back here for all the latest buzz, news and reactions from our ESPN NBA insiders, with the latest info at the top:

Quick links:

Free agency grades | Trade grades

Trade tracker | Transactions

Depth charts | Trade machine | More

Sept. 25

What's next for Curry and the Warriors?

Stephen Curry's two-year, $116 million extension made him the first player in NBA history to amass $600 million in career on-court earnings.

The deal has also put the Golden State Warriors in a position to have extra spending power next summer.

By Curry taking $10 million less than the maximum allowed, the Warriors project to have nearly $38 million in cap space in 2027. Golden State could increase its projection to $55 million if center Kristaps Porzingis is waived in the offseason. Porzingis' $20 million salary for next season is guaranteed for $3 million.

For Golden State to have ample room, forwards Draymond Green and Jimmy Butler III would need to sign elsewhere or at a significantly lesser salary. Both players are free agents next summer.

Both salary projections include the $17 million free agent hold of guard Brandin Podziemski. The former first-round pick is eligible until Oct. 19 to extend his contract. -- Bobby Marks

Grizzlies waive D'Angelo Russell

The Memphis Grizzlies have waived D'Angelo Russell, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania. Russell has made one All-Star team during his career and was selected No. 2 in the 2015 NBA draft.

Sept. 23

Sources: Status of Mavs big man Lively up in air

Dallas Mavericks center Dereck Lively II has not been cleared for training camp and his status for the start of the regular season has yet to be determined as he continues to recover from right foot surgery, sources told ESPN's Tim MacMahon.

After playing a key role as a rookie in the Mavericks' run to the 2024 NBA Finals, Lively's promising career has been derailed by recurring problems with his right foot, which has been surgically repaired twice in the last 14 months.

Lively is ramping up toward being cleared for basketball activity, sources said, emphasizing that the team is not discouraged by his progress. Dallas begins training camp on Saturday.

articles.headline: Man City chairman on club's Premier League charges case: 'Nothing has changed'
articles.description: Manchester City chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak has said "nothing has changed" regarding the club's ongoing legal battle with the Premier League.
articles.headlineJa: マンC会長、プレミアリーグの違反疑惑判決について「何も変わっていない」
articles.descriptionJa: マンチェスター・シティのカルドゥーン・アル・ムバラク会長は、プレミアリーグと進行中の法的闘争について「何も変わっていない」と述べ、「クラブの無実を証明するという我々の確信と意志は、これが始まった当初と変わらず強固だ」と付け加えました。
articles.body:
Manchester City chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak has said "nothing has changed" regarding the club's ongoing legal battle with the Premier League, adding "our confidence and intent in proving the club's innocence is just as strong as when this began."

City are expected to be found guilty on the vast majority of charges of financial breaches in their legal case with the Premier League, a source confirmed to ESPN.

In a statement on Friday, City didn't deny the guilty verdicts and said that the process "remains ongoing."

When contacted by ESPN on Friday, the Premier League said it wouldn't comment on a "private and confidential process."

It is expected that City -- who could face anything from a fine to a points deduction or even expulsion from the Premier League by way of punishment -- will appeal any guilty verdict.

Sources: Premier League clubs seeking legal advice over Man City charges

Al Mubarak's statement read: "I have been part of this Club for 18 years. I have had the privilege to stand with you in the Etihad, at Wembley, and in Istanbul. This Club matters to me, and you have shown and told me -- time and time again -- how much Manchester City matters to you," he said in a statement published on City's website.

"This is why I am writing to you today. Following Friday's media reporting, many of you will have spent your evening answering questions and responding to messages from friends, family and colleagues. So have I. Here's what I said to my family: The Premier League process still has a long way to run, and our confidence and intent in proving the Club's innocence is just as strong as when this began.

"There are so many things that I would like to be able to share with you to help you understand why we feel so confident in our position. But the strict confidentiality of the legal process and our determination to respect it means I cannot do that at the moment. Even this letter underwent several legal checks to make sure it complies.

"I ask you to please carefully read the statement below, which we gave on Friday, and the statement we issued in February 2023. Every word matters and holds true.

"While some people have been quick to reach their own conclusions, and there is so much noise swirling around us, nothing has changed. We have faced challenges together before and have prevailed. There remain many who want to undermine the momentum of our Club. We will not give them that opportunity.

"We have some exciting moments to look forward to after this international break. We travel to Anfield in a fortnight, and then host Paris St Germain in the Champions League back at Etihad Stadium -- moments that give us an opportunity to celebrate the strength of the Manchester City family.

"Thank you, as always, for your constant support."

articles.headline: Rio field gets final touches, 'no need to worry' NFL says
articles.description: NFL field director Nick Pappas said Saturday that the league has made additional improvements to the Rio field and that "things check out" ahead of Sunday's game between the Ravens and Cowboys.
articles.headlineJa: リオのフィールドが最終調整へ、NFLは「心配はいらない」と表明
articles.descriptionJa: NFLのフィールドディレクターであるニック・パパス氏は土曜日、日曜日に開催されるレイブンズ対カウボーイズの試合を前に、リーグがリオのフィールドに追加の改善を施しており、「問題はない」と語った。
articles.body:
RIO DE JANEIRO -- Workers were still trimming the turf at Maracana Stadium on Saturday, less than 30 hours before the NFL's first game in Rio de Janeiro, which is between the Dallas Cowboys and the Baltimore Ravens.

Some were using scissors to level the high grass, an effort that should end hours before the game.

The Maracana's turf has been a concern for almost two weeks due to its poor shape amid a long season in Brazilian soccer. Local clubs, Flamengo and Fluminense, play there at least once a week.

Maracana workers were using mows and scissors, big and small, to perfect the turf for the game.

On Friday, the executive director of the NFL Players Association said both the NFL and the players' union have had experts monitoring the field conditions for Sunday's game. The union's experts are worried about loose turf leading to too much slipping.

Concerns are about the turf's traction and stability, which made the NFL reinforce its stitching. Earlier this week, field director Nick Pappas said he was confident players will have no trouble.

On Saturday, Pappas told journalists that the NFL made additional improvements since the union's concerns were raised.

"Things check out," Pappas said. "No need to worry."

The NFL has been playing in Brazil since 2024, but the two previous games were at the 48,000-seat NeoQuimica Arena in Sao Paulo. In the first year of the Brazil game, its turf was also criticized and forced players of the Philadelphia Eagles and the Green Bay Packers to change their cleats to stop slipping.

The Maracana field is 100% natural grass, while the NeoQuimica Arena has a mixture between natural and synthetic that footballers in Brazil deem to be the country's best pitch.

The Cowboys and Ravens began their preparations in Rio on Friday following roughly 10-hour flights and are expected to have their first visit to the stadium later on Saturday.

Their game Sunday will be one of a record nine international contests on the NFL schedule this season.

Outside the Maracana, locals and tourists seem to be keener to go to the beach at 80 degrees on Saturday than preparing for Sunday's game. Unlike Sao Paulo, Rio has a more touristic atmosphere that has drawn a new batch of football followers from South America.

"I came because of the NFL game, but I also came because of Rio," said Chilean tourist Juan Olmedo, 61, a fan of the Denver Broncos. "This game being here has that extra element it didn't have in Sao Paulo. Those who went to Sao Paulo were there for the game and not much else."

Tourist spots such as Sugar Loaf Mountain and the statue of Christ the Redeemer also welcomed American and local fans who are attending the game Sunday.

articles.headline: Man City verdict will leave a stain and stench on a Premier League era
articles.description: Manchester City are expected to be found guilty of almost all 115 financial charges against them. It means an era of English soccer is now tarnished with multiple asterisks.
articles.headlineJa: マンCへの判決はプレミアリーグの一時代に汚点と悪臭を残すだろう
articles.descriptionJa: マンチェスター・シティは、問われている115件の財務違反疑惑のほぼ全てで有罪と認定されると予想されています。これは、イングランドサッカーの一時代が数々の注釈（アスタリスク）で汚されることを意味しています。
articles.body:
It was one of the Premier League's most iconic moments: May 2014 and Steven Gerrard, Liverpool's heroic captain, finally lifts the Premier League trophy alongside manager Brendan Rodgers, who ended the club's quarter-century wait to become champions of England once again. What a story.

England's fallen giants were back on their perch, and Gerrard, the greatest player never to win a title medal, was able to put the seal on a glorious career with the one major honor missing from his collection. Except it didn't happen. Just like Jose Mourinho winning his fourth Premier League title with Manchester United didn't happen four years later.

Perhaps in a parallel universe Liverpool are listed as 2013-14 Premier League champions and United in 2017-18, but in the real world, Manchester City came out on top on both occasions and on many more. But did they really?

The news that City are expected to be found guilty of 114 of the 115 charges related to breaching Premier League financial regulations between 2009 and 2018 -- neither City nor the Premier League deny the verdict of the independent panel -- means that everything they achieved during that period is now in question. City have consistently denied all the charges and are expected to appeal the verdict.

Forget the asterisks next to those title wins and cup triumphs -- those moments that have been imprinted forever on the fabric of English football. The imprints are still there -- they will never go away -- but neither will the stain and the stench of being found guilty of breaking the rules -- cheating -- to claim their own glorious moments and, just as importantly, deny others from experiencing them.

So next time you see a replay of Sergio Aguero's famous title-winning goal in the final seconds of the 3-2 win against Queen's Park Rangers on the final day of the 2011-12 season, ask yourself whether it is valid. Or more likely, the footage becomes nothing more than the Premier League's version of Ben Johnson sprinting to gold in the 1988 Olympics 100-meter final or any of the seven consecutive Tour de France wins by Lance Armstrong between 1999 and 2005.

Johnson and Armstrong were both unmasked as drug cheats and stripped of their titles. That may yet happen to City when the Premier League rolls out its sanctions for the industrial scale breaches that the club has been found guilty of -- massive fines and points deductions which could lead to relegation are likely -- but the problem is that nobody really remembers who came second in an unfair race.

Who did Armstrong beat into second place in those seven successive wins? Good luck answering that without using Wikipedia. But for those like Gerrard, Rodgers and Mourinho, finishing second to City had its costs and real-life consequences.

Gerrard would retire without ever having won the Premier League, and he has since admitted that his slip in a 2-0 home defeat against Chelsea, which tilted the title race in City's favour, still haunts him every day.

articles.body:
Arsenal and Liverpool have identified Brentford's Kevin Schade as a potential addition to their squads, while the rest of Europe chases new center back options.

Join us for the latest transfer news and rumors from around the globe.

Transfers home page | Men's summer grades | Women's grades

Trending rumors

- There is increasing interest in Brentford winger Kevin Schade from Arsenal and Liverpool, according to Sky Sports. Brentford have held initial talks with the Germany international about extending his contract to see off that interest, with the aforementioned pair being the most serious about signing the 24-year-old when the summer transfer window drew to a close, although Chelsea and Tottenham Hotspur are also admirers. Schade has entered the last two years of his current deal and Brentford are keen to offer him improved terms.

- Inter Milan center back Alessandro Bastoni has re-emerged as a transfer option for Barcelona, while Chelsea, Liverpool and Manchester City also retain an interest in him, according to TEAMtalk. The 27-year-old was the topic of serious interest during the summer, but Inter remained firm on their valuation of close to £70 million for the Italy international. Chelsea would benefit from his ability to play in a back three, while Liverpool and City are looking at him as they prepare to eventually lose Virgil van Dijk and Rúben Dias.

- Liverpool, Chelsea and Manchester City are all keen on a potential deal for versatile Atlético Madrid midfielder Marcos Llorente, whose contract expires in the summer, according to TEAMtalk. Madrid are in talks with the 31-year-old over fresh terms and there is confidence within the Spanish club that an agreement will be reached. The situation has still attracted interest from the Premier League, with the trio of giants assessing whether Llorente could become available.

- Real Madrid are keeping an eye on Stuttgart center back Finn Jeltsch, reports Spanish newspaper AS. Madrid have signed Dean Huijsen and Ibrahima Konaté in the last two summer transfer windows but continue their efforts to strengthen the heart of their defence, and they are now monitoring several players from around the world. Jeltsch, 20, received his first Germany call-up from Jürgen Klopp this international window having joined Stuttgart from Nurnberg in January 2025.

- Liverpool are very satisfied with Ronald Araújo during his loan from Barcelona and could trigger their option to permanently sign the defender for €55 million, reports Spanish outlet Mundo Deportivo. The Uruguay international has played seven matches for the Reds, five of those coming as a starter, but he is already convincing the club and Andoni Iraola. The versatility displayed by the 27-year-old to play both right-back and centre-back has also caught the eye.
